Plot differential-abundance results

Source: R/mp_diff.R
mp_diff.Rd

Visualises differential-abundance results as a volcano, MA, forest or ranked-dot plot, as a heatmap of fold changes across contrasts, or – when several methods were run – as a consensus matrix showing where the methods agree. Results from mp_run_da(), DESeq2, ALDEx2 and ANCOM-BC/ANCOM-BC2 are parsed automatically; any other tool can be supplied as a data frame with explicit column mappings, and a named list of results from different tools is stacked for comparison.

Usage

mp_diff(
  result,
  plot.type = c("volcano", "ma", "forest", "dot", "heatmap", "consensus", "zeros",
    "concordance"),
  fc.threshold = 1,
  p.threshold = 0.05,
  y.value = c("padj", "pvalue"),
  label.top = 10,
  color.up = "#B2182B",
  color.down = "#2166AC",
  color.ns = "grey75",
  result2 = NULL,
  method.names = c("Method 1", "Method 2"),
  contrast = NULL,
  robust.only = TRUE,
  top.n = 30,
  feature = NULL,
  log2fc = NULL,
  pvalue = NULL,
  padj = NULL,
  mean = NULL,
  lfcSE = NULL,
  theme = NULL,
  ...,
  plot.title = NULL,
  plot.subtitle = NULL,
  plot.caption = NULL,
  font.size = getOption("micropubr.font.size", 11),
  interactive = FALSE,
  return.data = FALSE,
  verbose = getOption("micropubr.verbose", FALSE)
)

Arguments

result

A differential-abundance result: the output of mp_run_da(), a DESeqResults object, an ALDEx2 data frame, an ANCOM-BC(2) result list, a generic data frame (see feature/log2fc/pvalue/padj), or a named list of any of these (one per method, e.g. list(DESeq2 = res1, ALDEx2 = res2)).

plot.type

One of "volcano", "ma", "forest", "dot", "heatmap" (fold change of significant taxa across contrasts), "consensus" (agreement across methods), "zeros" (ANCOM-BC2 structural zeros) or "concordance" (fold changes of two methods against each other).

fc.threshold

Absolute log2 fold-change cut-off for significance.

p.threshold

Adjusted p-value cut-off.

y.value

For volcano plots, plot -log10() of "padj" (default) or "pvalue" on the y-axis.

label.top

Number of most-significant features to label per panel.

color.up, color.down, color.ns

Colours for enriched, depleted and non-significant features.

result2

A second result (same parsing rules) for plot.type = "concordance". Not needed when result already holds exactly two methods.

method.names

Length-2 labels for the two methods in a concordance plot.

contrast

Optional character vector of contrasts (as in the contrast column, e.g. "Treatment vs Control", or an ANCOM-BC2 term such as "groupTreatment") to keep.

robust.only

Treat significant features that fail ANCOM-BC2's pseudo-count sensitivity analysis as not significant (the default, which matches ANCOM-BC2's diff_robust). Results without sensitivity information are unaffected.

top.n

Maximum number of features in forest, dot, heatmap and consensus plots (the most significant are kept; per panel for forest and dot plots).

feature, log2fc, pvalue, padj, mean, lfcSE

Optional column-name overrides when result is a generic data frame.

theme

A ggplot2 theme; defaults to the active theme (see mp_set_defaults(), otherwise mp_theme_publication()).

...

Additional arguments passed to the point geom.

plot.title, plot.subtitle, plot.caption

Optional labels.

font.size

Base font size.

interactive

If TRUE, return an interactive plotly widget instead of a static ggplot (requires plotly). See mp_alpha().

return.data

If TRUE, return the parsed differential-abundance data frame (with a direction column) instead of a plot; for plot.type = "consensus", the per-feature consensus table.

verbose

Print the detected result type and counts.

Value

A ggplot object, a plotly widget when interactive = TRUE, or a data frame when return.data = TRUE.

Details

Results with several contrasts (multi-group designs) or several methods are drawn as facets. ANCOM-BC(2) fold changes, which are natural logarithms, are converted to log2. Taxa that ANCOM-BC2 classifies as structural zeros (absent from a whole group) are not tested; they are counted in the subtitle and shown by plot.type = "zeros". When results carry ANCOM-BC2's pseudo-count sensitivity analysis, taxa that fail it are not counted as significant (as in ANCOM-BC2's own diff_robust output); they are counted in the subtitle and marked in heatmaps. With robust.only = FALSE they are kept and drawn as open symbols.

See also

mp_run_da() to run the analysis.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  feature = paste0("ASV", 1:50),
  log2FC = rnorm(50, sd = 2),
  pvalue = runif(50)^2,
  padj = p.adjust(runif(50)^2, "BH")
)
mp_diff(df, plot.type = "volcano")
